text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Wednesday morning newspapers.
- Parliamentary parties have not yet agreed on the strategy regarding Slovenia's bid to join the European Union as soon as possible.
- Parliament rejected an extra tax on new cars.
- Italian tenor Luciano Pavarotti arrived in Slovenia to hold his first ever concert in the country on Friday.
- Police said the June accident during a rescue exercise in the Slovenian Alps during which five rescuers were killed was not caused by a deliberate human mistake therefore noone will be prosecuted.
- Nova Ljubljanska Banka and Nova Kreditna Banka Maribor have to name new management boards by Monday following the end of their rehabilitation process a month ago.
- Furniture producer Alples went into bankruptcy due to high debts, Slovenia's Development Fund said.
- Paper maker Goricane is looking for an investor to take over 80 percent of the factory and help the firm out of financial problems.
- Unlisted bank Koper said it would like to purchase 15 percent of a smaller bank M Banka. The purchase needs to be approved by the Bank of Slovenia.
- The blue-chip SBI stock index jumped over six percent on Wednesday after the Bank of Slovenia relaxed foreign investment rules.
